topics.label: Lecture framing and the cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the learning outcomes and introduces the hallmarks framework that will organise the lecture.

topics.label: Deregulation of extracellular growth and survival signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in pathways that interpret extracellular signals make cancer cells proliferate and survive without normal regulation.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted cell maturation contributes to cancer, using blood-cell lineages and intestinal epithelial renewal as examples.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how changes in p53 signalling and the balance of apoptotic regulators allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and cancer-cell immortalisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how cancer cells bypass it by reactivating telomerase.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and the mutation-driven hallmarks recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of mutation-driven loss of growth control by establishing the protective role of cellular stress responses before the transition to more complex tumour behaviours.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism characterises cancer and can reinforce its development.

topics.label: Angiogenesis as a requirement for tumour growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the angiogenic switch supplies growing tumours with the perfusion needed to expand beyond oxygen-diffusion limits.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and establishment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells spread from a primary tumour and what determines whether that spread produces detectable secondary tumours.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture's learning goals and shared hallmarks framework before offering further reading and inviting questions.
